text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Palestinian President Arafat backtracks on terms for last troop pullback.
- Syria blames Israel for bombing.
- Hebron gunman Friedman, fellow soldier remanded.
- United States warns Americans of terrorist attacks in Israel.
- Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition problems intensify over Hebron deal.
- ECI Telecom completes $100 million private placement.
- Transportation study: open-skies policy saved $40 million.
- Jerusalem Bank gets license for dollar deposits.
GLOBES
- Netanyahu signals to Bank of Israel Governor Frenkel: 'interest and exchange rates will be determined by our budget actions.'.
HAARETZ
- At least nine dead in Damascus bombing; Israel blamed.
- Palestinian sources: Arafat told U.S. envoy Ross 'there are more burning issues than signing the agreement'.
- Suspicion: Friedman belonged to underground cell which planned series of attacks on Arabs.
- Ports Authority presents plan for train line between Gaza Strip and West Bank.
- Ten percent drop in revenues from land sales after tender cancellations.
- Tower semiconductor in European contacts to found factory in Israel.
MAARIV
- Israel rejects Syrian accusations Mossad blew up bus.
- Israel: Arafat raises new demands, delays agreement.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Friedman also planned attack on Temple Mount; third soldier investigated.
- Ministers threaten to oppose Hebron deal if Netanyahu commits to further redeployments in West Bank.
- American push for Netanyahu-Arafat meeting Saturday night.
